14|record describing scenes that no longer exist and the new scenes are never
15|resplit. Also `--step segment --force` then `--step classify` (no force)
16|reuses an analysis of the old scenes.

19|1. One helper module, pipeline/freshness.ts (replace pipeline/cache.ts; move
20|   or delete it and update callers):
21|   - `fingerprint(value: unknown): string` = sha256 hex (first 16 chars) of
22|     JSON.stringify(value). Callers pass plain arrays/objects in a fixed field
23|     order so it is deterministic.
24|   - `decide(force: boolean, recorded: string | undefined, current: string):
25|     { reuse: boolean; reason: string }` — reuse only when !force and
26|     recorded === current. Reasons: "forced", "no previous output",
27|     "inputs changed", "inputs unchanged".

29|     `{ recorded, current }` for that step (pure reads, no clients), plus
30|     `planSteps(dir, steps, force)` used by the dry run (below).
31|   Every step calls `decide` with its own pair; no other skip logic remains.

33|   - ingest: unchanged (its frozen textVersion rule stays as is).
34|   - segment: current = book.textVersion; recorded = scenes.json textVersion.
35|   - classify: current = fingerprint of scenes.json scenes (id, ch, start_n,
36|     end_n, title, summary, characters); recorded =
37|     analysis.json `provenance.input`. Classify writes `provenance.input`.
38|     It carries the old `provenance.resplit` only when that record's `input`
39|     equals the fingerprint of its new scenes' ranges (see resplit); else
40|     drops it.
41|   - resplit: current = fingerprint of analysis.json scene ranges (id,
42|     start_n, end_n); recorded = analysis.json `provenance.resplit.input`.
43|     Resplit writes `provenance.resplit.input` = fingerprint of the ranges it
44|     WROTE (its output is a fixed point: rerunning on its own output reuses),
45|     and also writes analysis `provenance.input` = classify fingerprint of
46|     the scenes.json it wrote, so a later classify reuses.
47|   - cluster: current = fingerprint of analysis scenes (id, final);
48|     recorded = music-clusters.json `provenance.input`. Cluster writes it.
49|   Missing or unparsable files/fields -> recorded undefined -> redo.

51|   one line per selected step, e.g. `classify: reuse (inputs unchanged)` or

53|   writes nothing and makes no network calls (ingest prints `ingest: not checked
54|in dry run (frozen textVersion rule)`). In a multi-step plan, once a step would redo, every later
55|   selected step prints `redo (upstream step redoes)`.
56|4. Current Oz data (data/books/oz, 151 scenes) has no recorded keys yet and
57|   must stay valid and be reused. Stamp it once: with a throwaway tsx
58|   one-liner (do not commit the script) compute the keys with the new
59|   helper and add ONLY analysis.json `provenance.input`,
60|   `provenance.resplit.input` and music-clusters.json `provenance.input`,
61|   writing JSON exactly the way the pipeline writes it
62|   (`${JSON.stringify(obj)}\n`). Nothing else in those files may change;
63|   check that with a script comparing old vs new parsed objects minus the new
64|   fields, and show the result. scenes.json and book.json do not change.
65|5. Tests (vitest, tmpdirs and fake clients like pipeline/resplit.test.ts and
66|   pipeline/classify.test.ts):
67|   - decide/fingerprint unit cases.
68|   - the --force sequence: segment forced with new boundaries -> classify
69|     without force redoes; classify forced -> resplit does NOT skip and the
70|     stale resplit record is dropped; resplit on its own output reuses;
71|     cluster redoes when finals change and reuses otherwise.
72|   - a full unforced rerun over unchanged files reuses every step and calls
73|     no client (fake clients that throw if called).
74|   - planSteps over the real data/books/oz returns reuse for segment,
75|     classify, resplit, cluster.
76|   Existing tests stay green; adjust only what the new provenance field
77|   legitimately changes.
78|6. Docs: a short docs/tasks/19-step-freshness.md (the rule table above, the
79|   dry-run command, the stamp) and one line in BUILT_DURING_HACKATHON.md;
80|   update the pipeline/build.ts usage comment and string.
81|

84|--dry-run` and paste its output in your final message (it must say reuse for
85|all four steps after ingest).
86|

89|hook with message "One freshness rule per pipeline step" and trailer
90|"Co-authored-by: Muse Code (Meta) <muse-code@agents.noreply.invalid>".

# Git source-control safety

The working tree belongs to the user. Make the change, leave it visible, and
let them decide what becomes history.

## Never without an explicit ask

The user must have asked for that exact write in this session, in their own
words. An explicit request to create a new commit counts anywhere in the user's
own task text, but it is not a request to amend, push, or tag. Finishing a task
without that request does not authorize a history write.

- `commit`, `commit --amend`, `push`, `tag`, `rebase`, `cherry-pick`, `revert`,
  `merge`, branch deletion, `reset --hard`, path restore, and `clean -f` all
  require an explicit ask.
- Never publish merely because publication would be useful.

## Before an authorized discard

Recovery is insurance, not authorization. A save never expands what the user
allowed you to delete or overwrite.

When the user explicitly authorized an operation that may discard or broadly
overwrite workspace changes, and the workspace is an ordinary Git checkout:

1. After `muse.read_skill` gives the physical Git skill package path, run:

   ```bash

2. Keep the printed `refs/tbh/recovery/...` value in your handoff, then perform
   only the exact authorized operation.
3. If the save fails or the workspace is unsupported, stop before destruction
   and ask the user.

To recover that saved tree later, run:

```bash

```

index in place, and restores the selected snapshot into the worktree. The ref
also retains distinct staged bytes when the same path had later worktree edits.
Read those staged bytes with `git show '<recovery-ref>^2:<path>'`; the recovery
commit's second parent is the saved index tree. Ignored files are not saved;
restore refuses an ignored-path collision rather than overwrite data it could

tool that requires a clean tree, are also fine when the original state is put
back afterward.

- Do not use a broad add in a tree you did not clean; name the files you changed.
- Do not initialize a repository inside vendored, build, data, or existing
  source-control trees.

  stashing, or deleting the user's files; clean up only scratch you created
  and say the user's files remain.
- Do not hand-edit generated files; change their source of truth.
- Scratch repositories under a temporary directory are yours to experiment in.

## Locks and corrupt state

A Git lock usually means another process is writing. Never kill the holder on
your own initiative. Wait, inspect the holder read-only, use that tool's normal
stop mechanism, or report the block. Never delete a lock without proving no
live process owns it, and never respond to index corruption by deleting state
and committing anyway.

Never commit or push while status reports changes you did not make and cannot
explain.

## If you already made an unwanted write

Say so plainly and stop. Do not attempt more history surgery without direction.
